guardian.description:
Shipment discovered at airport in Monrovia and valued at £14.2m had been falsely declared as seasoning cubes

Authorities in Liberia have charged five suspects over one of the largest drug seizures in the country’s history, after police found more than 200kg of cocaine falsely declared as Maggi seasoning cubes.

guardian.title: Archaeologists uncover ancient Byzantine city in Egypt’s western desert
guardian.description:
Well-preserved fourth-century quarters reveal details of daily life, urban development and economic activities

Archaeologists in Egypt have uncovered a well-preserved Byzantine-era city in the western desert.

The fourth-century quarters had residential and religious structures, including a basilica-style church in the Dakhla oasis. Archaeologists also found coins, pottery fragments and tools.

guardian.description:
Arrival of endangered cats, including rare white cub, revitalises team straining under fuel and medicine shortages

For the Cuban zookeeper Ángel Cordero, the sight of four Bengal ⁠tiger cubs playing in a cage at the Cuban national zoo is a small miracle on an island stifled by shortages ⁠of fuel, medicine and ⁠days-long power outages.

The ​birth of these endangered big cats – including an exceedingly rare white tiger – has revitalised a team of zoo workers, he said.

rfi.description: Four Ugandan farmers filed a case against the East African Crude Oil Pipeline (EACOP) at the UK's High Court on Tuesday, seeking to have Ugandan constitutional, environmental and climate law applied to EACOP Ltd, the UK-registered company financing the project

rfi.title: Trump lashes out at NATO allies over Greenland and Iran, targeting Spain
rfi.description: United States President Donald Trump lashed out at NATO allies on Wednesday at the organisations's summit in Ankara, as the fallout from his war on Iran threatened to overshadow the gathering.

rfi.title: Macron says Syria must not be destabilised after bombs wound 18
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron warned on Tuesday that Syria must not be destabilised after twin bomb attacks near the Damascus hotel where he spent the night, during a landmark state visit to a country emerging from years of civil war.

rfi.title: Kenya journalist escapes abduction after criticism of president, says CPJ
rfi.description: The Committee to Protect Journalists has called for an investigation into the attempted kidnapping of a senior journalist in Kenya, which followed angry criticism of his newspaper by President William Ruto.

rfi.title: Submarine missile test puts China's Pacific ambitions on display
rfi.description: A Chinese submarine test-fired a "strategic" missile carrying a dummy warhead into the Pacific Ocean on Monday, Beijing said, prompting immediate condemnation across the region.

rfi.title: Egyptian football chiefs hit out at World Cup referees following last-16 exit
rfi.description: The Egyptian Football Association (EFA) on Wednesday lodged a formal complaint with World Cup organisers Fifa over the officiating during the team's defeat to defending champions Argentina on Tuesday in the last-16 at the 2026 World Cup.

rfi.title: Greenland 'not for sale', Danish PM says at NATO summit
rfi.description: Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said Wednesday that Greenland was "not for sale" following remarks by President Donald Trump suggesting the territory should be controlled by Washington and not Copenhagen.

rfi.title: Oil prices continue to rally as US and Iran step up mutual attacks
rfi.description: Oil prices jumped more than 3 percent on Wednesday as the Middle East crisis burst back into the spotlight, with United States and Iranian forces exchanging strikes after attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, fuelling fresh supply fears.

rfi.title: Switzerland beat Colombia on penalties to set up last-eight date with Argentina
rfi.description: Switzerland beat Colombia in a penalty shootout on Tuesday to advance to the last eight at the World Cup for the first time since 1954. They will play Argentina on Saturday in Kansas City.

rfi.title: TotalEnergies to discuss Syria offshore exploration, still wary of insecurity
rfi.description: TotalEnergies CEO Patrick Pouyanné said security concerns still rule out a return to onshore oil operations, but confirmed the French company is rebuilding its Iraq-Syria oil transit routes.

rfi.title: Le Pen confirms  presidential bid after Paris appeals court upholds conviction
rfi.description: The leader of France's far-right National Rally, Marine Le Pen, said on Tuesday she would run for president next year after an embezzlement conviction was confirmed on appeal, a ruling she said she would challenge before the country's highest court.

rfi.title: Climate justice in Africa: floods, fossil fuels and the fightback
rfi.description: This week in Spotlight on Africa, we look at climate change, environmental justice and the challenges of adaptation. While Europe's heatwaves make headlines, temperatures are also climbing across Africa, with parts of the Sahel approaching 50°C. West Africa is also experiencing severe flooding caused by climate change. Yet Africa is also a source of innovation and solutions, as we'll be discussing today.

rfi.title: Macron condemns Paraguayan senator's racist remarks as Mbappé hits back
rfi.description: Kylian Mbappé condemned a Paraguayan senator on Monday for making racist comments about him following France's World Cup victory over Paraguay, calling her "despicable" and "not worthy" of her position.

rfi.title: Argentina return from the brink to beat Egypt and reach World Cup quarter-finals
rfi.description: Argentina advanced to the last eight at the World Cup after recovering from a two-goal deficit to see off Egypt 3-2 on Tuesday.

rfi.title: EU warns France under-15 social media bill could breach European law
rfi.description: The European Commission has warned that a French bill that would ban children under the age of 15 from social media would infringe the European Union’s online content law by giving French regulators powers that go beyond the bloc’s legal framework.

rfi.title: NATO summit in Ankara tests unity as Ukraine war and Trump tensions loom
rfi.description: As NATO leaders gather in Ankara tomorrow, Tuesday, the alliance faces a stark test of unity, burden-sharing and strategic clarity, with the war in Ukraine, transatlantic tensions and Middle East instability all pressing heavily on the agenda.

rfi.title: De Ketelaere shines as Belgium trump US to advance to World Cup quarter-finals
rfi.description: Charles de Ketelaere scored twice as Belgium swept past the United States 4-1 on Monday night to reach the last eight at the World Cup.

rfi.title: European football chiefs hit out at Fifa move to lift ban on US star Balgoun
rfi.description: European football's governing body Uefa on Monday lashed out at the decision of World Cup organisers Fifa to suspend the immediate one-match ban of the United States striker Folarin Balogun following the intervention of US President Donald Trump.

euronews.title: Dangerous jellyfish in Germany: where swimmers should take care
euronews.description: As sea temperatures rise, jellyfish are once again a familiar sight on many beaches, even in the Baltic and North Seas. A brief look at common species in popular holiday regions.

euronews.title: Archaeology: 18 ancient tombs in Egypt yield 'golden tongue' amulets
euronews.description: New excavations at Marina El Alamein, ancient Leukaspis, reveal 18 Ptolemaic and Roman tombs with rare amulets and gold sheets used in “golden tongue” rites, enriching Mediterranean archaeology.

euronews.title: Iran launches retaliatory strikes on Gulf states as Trump warns US bombing could get 'much worse'
euronews.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they had struck US military bases in Bahrain and Kuwait in response to fresh American strikes. They also warned their responses would expand to other bases across the region if US attacks were repeated.

euronews.title: March for peace in memory of the victims of the Srebrenica genocide
euronews.description: Several thousand people gathered in Bosnia and Herzegovina on Wednesday to take part in a peace march in memory of the victims of the genocide and the survivors who fled the town of Srebrenica in July 1995.

euronews.title: Trump skips new Air Force One on return from Turkey NATO summit
euronews.description: Asked during a press conference whether the change was for security reasons related to Iran, Trump sidestepped the question by talking about previous alleged assassination attempts by Tehran.

euronews.title: Tanks vs. tractors? Can the EU keep providing a political shield to farmers? MEPs debate in The Ring
euronews.description: Tough talks on the EU’s next long-term budget, Ukraine’s push for EU accession and skyrocketing fertiliser costs are putting European farmers under the political spotlight once more. Can the EU continue to appease them as it shifts its focus to defence and global trade? MEPs debate on The Ring.

euronews.title: Trump tempers fury with allies and ends 'tremendously successful' NATO summit on high note
euronews.description: European leaders showcased their surging defence spending at the summit as they looked to convince Trump they're making good on a pledge to ramp up budgets and take more responsibility for their own security.

euronews.title: 'Associating Islam with violence contradicts its true nature': Global Forum debates Islamic heritage
euronews.description: More than 70 international projects were launched at Uzbekistan's first Islamic Civilisation Forum, where delegates called for greater scientific cooperation, education and preservation of Islamic heritage.

euronews.title: Venezuela calls for release of frozen assets to help earthquake recovery efforts
euronews.description: Meanwhile, the United Nations launched an urgent appeal on Wednesday to raise €259 million for relief operations.

euronews.title: Economy: IMF forecasts modest growth for Italy, cuts estimates for France and Germany
euronews.description: The IMF has also lifted its 2026 global inflation forecast to 4.7%, citing rising energy and commodity prices and risks from tensions in the Middle East.

euronews.title: Barcelona sets new heat record of 40.5C, weather agencies say
euronews.description: Scientists say human-driven climate change is increasing the intensity, length and frequency of extreme weather events such as heatwaves.

euronews.title: Rescuers search for five missing people after deadly landslide in India's Kerala state
euronews.description: Experts say human-caused climate change is intensifying South Asia’s monsoons, which traditionally run from June to September and again from October to December.

euronews.title: Putting survivors at the heart of Europe's fight against child sexual abuse
euronews.description: A new EU Directive ensures that victims of child rape can report the crime until the age of 50 – establishing a minimum standard across all 27 Member States,  describes Jeroen Lenaers, MEP (Christian Democrats) in an OpEd for Euronews.

euronews.title: French watchdog orders Meta back to press payment talks after copyright deals expire
euronews.description: France’s competition authority warns Meta’s approach to copyright talks with news outlets could “seriously harm” the press

euronews.title: Thousands embark on Bosnia peace march to remember Srebrenica victims
euronews.description: Over 6,500 people took part in a peace march to remember the victims of the Srebrenica genocide and the survivors who walked for days to save their lives.

euronews.title: Do World Cup hydration breaks protect players in the heat?
euronews.description: Scientists are questioning whether FIFA's hydration breaks do enough to protect players competing in extreme heat. While some argue the breaks disrupt the game, researchers say longer cooling periods and active cooling measures may better reduce heat-related health risks.

euronews.title: ‘People admire scars’: MEPs fear Le Pen more than Bardella
euronews.description: The general feeling in the European Parliament is that the longstanding far-right leader has a better chance of becoming France’s president than her younger successor.

euronews.title: Spanish PM Sánchez says ties with US 'very positive' after Trump threat to cut all trade
euronews.description: Clashes with Trump and Israel have made Sánchez, one of the few remaining openly leftist voices in a Europe increasingly dominated by right-wing politics, a hero to many progressives around the world.

lemonde.title: Au sommet de l’OTAN, Donald Trump alterne menaces et effusions, rassure ses alliés et apporte un nouveau soutien à l’Ukraine
lemonde.description: En Turquie, le président américain, après avoir critiqué l’Espagne et rappelé ses visées sur le Groenland, a assuré de son engagement en faveur de la clause d’assistance mutuelle de l’Alliance et autorisé Kiev à produire sous licence des missiles Patriot.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, canicule : soixante-douze départements en vigilance orange jeudi ; jusqu’à 43 °C relevés dans l’Hérault par Météo-France mercredi
lemonde.description: Cinq départements supplémentaires passeront en vigilance orange canicule, à partir de jeudi midi. Météo-France estime que cet « épisode caniculaire sévère et durable » pourrait se prolonger « très probablement jusqu’au week-end prochain inclus ».

lemonde.title: Entre l’Iran et les Etats-Unis, la reprise des hostilités illustre la grande défiance de Téhéran vis-à-vis des négociations
lemonde.description: Les échanges de frappes des dernières heures donnent des arguments à la frange ultraconservatrice du régime théocratique, qui considère les discussions avec Washington comme criminelles. Le cessez-le-feu ne tient plus qu’à un fil.

lemonde.title: France-Maroc : la soif de revanche des Lions de l’Atlas, quatre ans après la demi-finale perdue au Qatar
lemonde.description: La sélection marocaine de football n’a battu la France qu’une seule fois, lors d’un tournoi amical, en mai 1998. Vingt-huit ans plus tard, ses supporteurs ont des raisons de croire en une victoire de leur équipe, plus forte que jamais, en quarts de finale du Mondial 2026.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : vote décisif pour Olivier Faure et le Parti socialiste en vue de désigner un candidat « social-démocrate »
lemonde.description: Les militants du PS se prononcent, jeudi, sur la méthode de départage de leur future tête d’affiche, mais la « primaire de la gauche » incluant les écologistes et les anciens « insoumis » n’est plus à l’ordre du jour.

lemonde.title: Meurtre de Mehdi Kessaci : l’enquête se resserre sur Amine Oualane, l’un des leaders de la DZ Mafia, et ses relais dans une prison de l’Ain
lemonde.description: Des enregistrements versés dans l’enquête sur le meurtre du petit frère du militant antidrogue Amine Kessaci laissent penser que l’un des leaders de la DZ Mafia est responsable du crime, organisé depuis la prison de Bourg-en-Bresse. Quatre nouveaux suspects ont été mis en examen, lundi 6 juillet.

lemonde.title: La contrôleuse générale des lieux de privation de liberté dénonce les « violences systémiques » pratiquées contre les détenus à la prison de Condé-sur-Sarthe
lemonde.description: Dans un rapport publié jeudi 9 juillet, l’autorité indépendante alerte sur une « logique d’intimidation et d’abus de pouvoir » des surveillants, dans le quartier de lutte contre la criminalité, mais aussi des propos racistes, au sein de la prison de l’Orne.

lemonde.title: Le mois de juin le plus chaud de l’histoire en Europe occidentale, selon l’institut Copernicus
lemonde.description: Des milliers de décès ont été liés à cette envolée des températures, principalement en France, en Espagne et en Belgique, et plus des deux tiers des Européens – soit 410 millions de personnes – ont subi des températures dépassant les 35 °C pendant la vague de chaleur du 15 au 30 juin.

lemonde.title: Les femmes enceintes et leurs bébés, particulièrement vulnérables face à l’épidémie d’Ebola dans l’est de la RDC
lemonde.description: Accouchements prématurés, hémorragies et morts fœtales intra utero : les femmes enceintes sont en première ligne de l’épidémie. Moins de 10 % des patientes contaminées survivent, selon les Nations unies.

lemonde.title: France Télévisions s’inscrit plus que jamais dans la stratégie « streaming first »
lemonde.description: L’annonce des programmes des chaînes publiques pour la rentrée a été l’occasion, pour la présidente Delphine Ernotte-Cunci et ses troupes, de revendiquer la primauté donnée à la diffusion des contenus sur le numérique.

lemonde.title: Inceste : une commission d’enquête parlementaire émet des propositions en faveur des « mères protectrices »
lemonde.description: La commission, qui fait le constat d’une absence de politique publique en matière d’inceste, préconise notamment de dépénaliser la non-représentation d’enfants et plaide en faveur d’une ordonnance de protection immédiate en cas de suspicion de violences incestueuses.

lemonde.title: En Europe, la crainte du retour de l’Allemagne comme puissance militaire
lemonde.description: En prévoyant de consacrer 3,5 % de son produit intérieur brut à sa défense d’ici à 2029, Berlin répond aux attentes de ses alliés, qui somment le pays depuis des années de prendre davantage ses responsabilités sur la scène internationale. Mais ce réarmement ravive de vieilles peurs, notamment en France, en Italie et en Pologne.

lemonde.title: Affaire E. Jean Carroll : un juge ordonne à Donald Trump de verser les 5 millions de dollars qu’il doit à l’autrice
lemonde.description: Cette décision fait suite au refus de la Cour suprême d’examiner le recours du président américain qui avait été reconnu coupable d’agression sexuelle et de diffamation contre l’ancienne journaliste et chroniqueuse, aujourd’hui âgée de 82 ans.

lemonde.title: Séismes au Venezuela : le bilan monte à 3 811 morts, la présidente demande au roi d’Angleterre le déblocage de l’or du pays
lemonde.description: Alors que les besoins humanitaires restent considérables, Caracas poursuit ses démarches pour obtenir la levée des restrictions sur ses avoirs gelés à l’étranger. Les Nations unies évaluent les pertes provoquées par les séismes à 6,7 milliards de dollars.

lemonde.title: Un trio de mathématiciens démontre la conjecture de Talagrand
lemonde.description: Un problème de géométrie mis à prix 2 000 dollars a été résolu grâce à des outils venus d’autres disciplines, aussi diverses que les probabilités, les mathématiques financières ou la théorie de l’information.

lemonde.title: Sahel : Sergueï Lavrov, ministre des affaires étrangères russe, en visite au Niger, dit vouloir poursuivre le « soutien » militaire aux juntes
lemonde.description: Lors d’un échange avec l’Alliance des Etats du Sahel, qui regroupe le Mali, le Niger et le Burkina Faso, le chef de la diplomatie russe et les leaders putschistes se sont accordés pour poursuivre « leur coopération dans les domaines politique, diplomatique, sécuritaire, économique et social ».

lemonde.title: « On peut se débarrasser de son stress ici » : à Oakland, loin de la Coupe du monde, le « pouvoir du football » au service des réfugiés
lemonde.description: L’organisation Soccer Without Borders est installée au sein d’un lycée de la ville californienne qui n’accueille que des migrants ou des réfugiés.

lemonde.title: Députés et sénateurs s’accordent sur une réforme du sport professionnel renforçant l’encadrement du football
lemonde.description: Le texte prévoit notamment un encadrement renforcé des droits télévisés, de la rémunération des dirigeants sportifs et de la multipropriété des clubs. Son adoption définitive par le Parlement est attendue le 21 juillet.

france24fr.title: Des échanges de frappes au Moyen-Orient, une escalade entre l'Iran et les États-Unis
france24fr.description: Depuis 22h mercredi, les médias iraniens ont rapporté une série de frappes sur l'Iran, "somme toute limitée" par rapport à ce qu'avait annoncé Donald Trump, estime Siavosh Ghazi, le correspondant de France 24 à Téhéran. Il rappelle que l'Iran, qui a riposté mercredi aux premières frappes américaines, est déterminé à conserver le contrôle sur le détroit d'Ormuz. Une question perdure : jusqu'où va aller l'escalade?

france24fr.title: En direct : le cessez-le-feu "fini", l'armée américaine dit avoir visé 90 cibles en Iran
france24fr.description: Nouvelle nuit de frappes au Moyen-Orient après que le cessez-le-feu ait volé en éclats, comme l'a commenté Donald Trump. Les Gardiens de la Révolution iraniens ont annoncé avoir frappé des bases américaines au Koweït et à Bahreïn en riposte à des frappes menées par Washington en Iran, et menacé d'étendre leurs attaques à d'autres pays de la région. L'armée américaine a, selon le Centcom, atteint 90 «cibles militaires», dont des systèmes de défense antiaérienne. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'arrivée fracassante des supporters français à Boston
france24fr.description: La veille du quart de finale France-Maroc, les supporters français ont fait une arrivée fracassante à Boston, où se jouera le match ce jeudi 9 juillet.

france24fr.title: La Russie poursuivra "son soutien" militaire aux États du Sahel, assure Sergueï Lavrov à Niamey
france24fr.description: À Niamey, le ministre russe des Affaires étrangères, Sergueï Lavrov, a participé mercredi à des consultations de "haut niveau" avec les chefs de la diplomatie du Mali, du Burkina et du Niger, réunis dans l'Alliance des États du Sahel (AES). Selon un communiqué, Moscou "a confirmé sa volonté de poursuivre son soutien au renforcement des capacités opérationnelles des forces armées de l'AES".

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis ont lancé de nouvelles frappes contre l'Iran, Donald Trump menace de "bien pire"
france24fr.description: L'armée américaine a procédé mercredi soir à une nouvelle série de frappes contre l'Iran. Donald Trump, qui a décrit le protocole d'accord conclu en juin comme "fini", a menacé Téhéran de frappes "bien pires" s'il continue ses attaques. L'armée américaine avait déjà mené, mardi soir, des frappes en Iran en réponse à l'attaque de pétroliers dans le détroit d'Ormuz. Les deux médiateurs, Qatar et Pakistan, ont appelé, à l'instar de l'ONU, à la désescalade.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le huitième de finale Égypte-Argentine était-il "truqué" en faveur de Messi ?
france24fr.description: Incroyable retournement de situation de l'Argentine face à l'Égypte : les Champions du monde en titre se sont imposés 3 buts à 2 dans les dix dernières minutes du match après avoir été menée 2 à 0 par les Pharaons. Depuis, l'Egypte ne décolère pas, dénonce un match truqué et du favoritisme envers l'Albiceleste. Info/Intox se lance dans une opération de fact-checking sportif pour démêler le vrai du faux d'un match sous haute tension.

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis vont retirer la Syrie de leur liste noire des États soutenant le terrorisme
france24fr.description: Le secrétaire d'État américain Marco Rubio a officiellement informé, mercredi, le Congrès de la décision du gouvernement de retirer la Syrie de leur liste noire des pays accusés de soutenir le terrorisme. Ce "pas historique de la part du président Trump" sera effectif dans 45 jours – sauf blocage des parlementaires.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : Le Président Diomaye Faye saisi le Conseil constitutionnel
france24fr.description: Au Sénégal, nouvelle dissension entre Bassirou Diomaye Faye et le Pastef. Le Président de la République a saisi le Conseil constitutionnel sur la réforme de la Constitution adoptée le 29 juin par l'Assemblée nationale. Cette réforme réduit les pouvoirs du chef de l'État tout en renforçant ceux de l'Assemblée.

france24fr.title: 🔴 L'armée américaine annonce avoir lancé de nouvelles frappes contre l'Iran, suivez notre direct
En Irak, une immense foule dit adieu à Ali Khamenei avant son inhumation en Iran
france24fr.description: Une grande foule a envahi, mercredi, les rues des villes saintes chiites de Najaf et Kerbala en Irak. Ces personnes ont accompagné le cortège funéraire de l'ancien Guide suprême iranien Ali Khamenei, avant qu'il ne soit inhumé dans son pays natal.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l’arbitrage France-Maroc fait déjà débat, la réaction de Deschamps
france24fr.description: L'arbitrage de France-Maroc fait déjà débat. La FIFA a désigné l'Argentin Facundo Tello pour diriger ce quart de finale du Mondial 2026, un choix très commenté. Interrogé en conférence de presse, Didier Deschamps a refusé d'alimenter la polémique et appelé à faire confiance au corps arbitral.

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis vont autoriser l'Ukraine à fabriquer des missiles Patriot
france24fr.description: À l'issue du sommet de l'Otan à Ankara, en Turquie, Donald Trump a indiqué mercredi qu'il allait autoriser l'Ukraine à fabriquer des missiles Patriot, de conception américaine, pour renforcer leurs défenses antiaériennes face à la Russie.

france24fr.title: Comment sauver l'OTAN ?
france24fr.description: Les pays membres de l'Otan ont affiché un front uni mercredi à Ankara, au terme d'un sommet marqué par les prises de position contrastées du président américain, qui a alterné entre vives critiques et un ton extraordinairement conciliant. Dans leur déclaration commune, les Alliés ont réaffirmé leur attachement "indéfectible" au principe de défense collective inscrit à l'article 5 du Traité de l'Atlantique Nord, pilier fondateur de l'Alliance.

france24fr.title: "L'Afrique renégate", un appel à la réappropriation intellectuelle du continent
france24fr.description: « L’Afrique a du potentiel. » Cette phrase, on l’entend depuis des décennies. Pourtant, le potentiel, sans vision ni action, reste une promesse qui ne se concrétise jamais. C’est le constat qui ouvre "L’Afrique renégate", un ouvrage qui questionne les modèles de développement du continent et invite l’Afrique à tracer sa propre voie. Son auteur était l’invité du Journal de l’Afrique ce mardi.

france24fr.title: Élevages décimés, récoltes réduites : l'agriculture forcée de s'adapter aux canicules ?
france24fr.description: Des millions de volailles mortes de chaud, un risque accru d’incendie pendant les moissons, des fruits cuits sur pied… Depuis dimanche 5 juillet, la France est traversée par une nouvelle vague de chaleur, la troisième, déjà, depuis le début de la canicule mi-mai. Ces épisodes précoces et rapprochés fragilisent élevages et cultures, forçant les agriculteurs à trouver des solutions d'urgence pour s’adapter.

france24fr.title: Condamnation de Marine Le Pen : la Cour de cassation se prononcera "au plus tard début avril 2027"
france24fr.description: La Cour de cassation a indiqué mercredi qu'elle devrait pouvoir statuer "au plus tard début avril 2027" sur le pourvoi de Marine Le Pen contre sa condamnation dans l'affaire des assistants d'eurodéputés du Front national (FN, ancêtre du RN). La Cour a toutefois prévenu que ce délai est assujetti à des "facteurs procéduraux".

france24fr.title: Tour de France, cinquième étape : le Néerlandais Olav Kooij remporte le sprint à Pau
france24fr.description: Le Néerlandais Olav Kooij a remporté, mercredi, la cinquième étape du Tour de France à Pau, à l'issue d'un sprint chaotique marqué par plusieurs chutes dans le final.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Marine Le Pen en campagne, jour 1
france24fr.description: Au lendemain de son annonce de candidature malgré sa condamnation en appel, Marine Le Pen a lancé sa campagne à La Flèche, aux côtés de Jordan Bardella.

Wetterprognose: Sommerwetter in NRW – bis zu 33 Grad am Samstag
Elbvertiefung: Der tägliche Newsletter aus Hamburg: Warum bei vielen Großprojekten gerade die Kosten steigen
zeit.description: Die Elbvertiefung am Donnerstag – mit einem langwierigen Versuch, Fluggastrechte geltend zu machen, einer Cafégründung in Bergedorf und Bussen, die seltener fahren

zeit.title: Irankrieg: US-Militär greift rund 90 Ziele im Iran an
zeit.description: Zum zweiten Mal binnen 24 Stunden haben die USA den Iran angegriffen. Trump droht: Sollte der Iran erneut Schiffe angreifen, könnte es »noch viel schlimmer werden«.

zeit.title: Stundenlange Löscharbeiten: Schrottberg in Salzgitter brennt seit Stunden
Die Lage im Überblick: USA und Iran eskalieren weiter - Geht der Krieg wieder los?
Notfallseelsorger nach Vorfall: Von Hund gebissen: Vierjähriges Kind stirbt
Kurzzeitige Fahrplanänderung: Ringbahn und S47 fahren heute Nacht nicht durch
Irankrieg: USA greifen 90 Ziele an, Revolutionsgarde attackiert US-Stützpunkte
zeit.description: Die zweite Nacht in Folge hat das US-Militär den Iran bombardiert. Donald Trump droht mit härteren Angriffen. Der US-Verbündete Kuwait meldet Beschuss. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Bis 35 Grad: Kühlen Kopf bewahren: Südwesten steht vor Hitzewochenende
Pete Hegseth: »Gott will es«
zeit.description: Das hat sich US-Verteidigungsminister Pete Hegseth auf den Bizeps tätowieren lassen. Woran glaubt Anführer der mächtigsten Armee der Welt?  Ein Treffen mit seinem Pastor

zeit.title: Trumps Korruption: Kommt er wirklich mit allem durch?
zeit.description: Noch müssen die Demokraten zuschauen, wie Trump seine Präsidentschaft zu Geld macht und Privates mit Politischem vermischt. Doch das könnte sich bald ändern.

zeit.title: Bundeswehr: Grüne und SPD für Abzug der Bundeswehrschiffe aus Nahem Osten
zeit.description: Der Irankrieg geht wieder weiter. Die Bundestagsfraktionen von Grünen und SPD fordern daher, die beiden in die Region entsandten Bundeswehrschiffe zurückzuholen.

zeit.title: Midterms in den USA: US-Demokrat Platner kündigt nach Missbrauchsvorwürfen Rückzug an
zeit.description: Der demokratische Senatskandidat Graham Platner tritt nach Missbrauchsvorwürfen nicht mehr bei den Zwischenwahlen an. Für die Demokraten ist das ein Rückschlag.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Erpresser überall: Die Diskussion um Medikamentenpreise läuft aus dem Ruder – zum Nachteil der Schweiz
nzz.description: Die Pharmaindustrie nutzt den Druck der Regierung Trump geschickt, um in Europa für teurere Arzneimittel zu lobbyieren. Statt sich nur darüber zu empören, muss die Schweiz klären, was sie eigentlich will.

nzz.title: Für den historischen WM-Erfolg brauchte es jeden Schweizer Nationalspieler. Aber das sind die fünf Säulen in Murat Yakins Erfolgsteam
nzz.description: Der erste Einzug in den WM-Viertelfinal seit 1954 gründet auf einer herausragenden Mannschaftsleistung. Diese Fussballer sind für das Funktionieren der Auswahl besonders wichtig.

nzz.title: Der Iran-Krieg eskaliert wieder. Was bedeutet das für die Region und die Weltwirtschaft? Drei Szenarien
nzz.description: Donald Trump hat die Verhandlungen mit Iran als nutzlos bezeichnet. Dennoch müssten die Parteien ein Interesse an einer Deeskalation haben. «NZZ Pro» präsentiert drei Szenarien, wie es nun weitergehen könnte.

nzz.title: Endlich wieder Weltklasse: Nach Jahren der Krise hofft Ägypten auf eine Wiedergeburt
nzz.description: Die Republik am Nil war einst die bestimmende Macht im Nahen Osten, ehe sie abstürzte. Nun will das Land an alte Grösse anknüpfen. Das dramatische WM-Spiel gegen Argentinien kam da gerade recht.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Nun sag, liebe Nato, wie hast du’s mit der Willenskraft?
nzz.description: Die westliche Allianz rüstet auf und beschwört am Gipfel in Ankara ihre Einheit. Aber die sicherheitspolitische Gretchenfrage bleibt unbeantwortet. Wäre die Nato im Ernstfall handlungsfähig? Im Moment spricht vieles dagegen.

nzz.title: Das Ende von Orbans «Lügenfabrik»: Ungarns staatlicher Sender entschuldigt sich und setzt Nachrichten aus
nzz.description: Der neue Regierungschef Peter Magyar reformiert die öffentlichrechtlichen Medien. Sie waren eine Bastion der Orban-Propaganda. Aber auch dessen restliches Medienimperium ist ins Wanken geraten.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «Physiotherapie ist nicht Wellness» – hinter dem Streit der Physiotherapeuten steckt mehr als ein Konflikt über Tarife
nzz.description: Eine Gruppe von Therapeuten hat sich vom Verband Physioswiss abgespalten. Christoph Landolt ist Verwaltungsrat bei Physiozentrum und Mitgründer des neuen Verbands Prophysio. Er sagt: Die moderne Physiotherapie sei heute politisch nicht gut genug repräsentiert.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Kevin Warsh im KI-Dilemma: Die grosse Hoffnung auf niedrigere Inflation muss warten
nzz.description: Der neue Fed-Chef propagierte einst, künstliche Intelligenz senke die Inflation und erlaube niedrigere Leitzinsen. Im Amt ist er deutlich zurückhaltender. Recht könnte er trotzdem behalten.

nzz.title: Die Cumulus-Kreditkarte war für Cembra das Hauptgeschäft: Nach einer Durststrecke hoffen Investoren auf ein rascheres Wachstum
nzz.description: Bei der Konsumkreditbank ist das «Buy now, pay later»-Geschäft nicht wie gewünscht gewachsen. Das soll sich nun wieder ändern.

nzz.title: Millionen hier, Millionen dort – mit den neuen EU-Verträgen wäre das Parlament beim Verteilen von Subventionen etwas weniger frei
nzz.description: In den Bereichen Strom und Verkehr soll die Schweiz die EU-Regeln übernehmen, wenn es um staatliche Beihilfen geht. Das sorgt für Unruhe im Parlament. Die Verwaltung beschwichtigt.

nzz.title: Der neue Börsenstar nach SpaceX: Südkoreas Speicherchip-Riese SK Hynix wagt das zweitgrösste Listing aller Zeiten
nzz.description: SK Hynix bringt Aktien im Wert von voraussichtlich 28 Milliarden Dollar an die amerikanische Tech-Börse Nasdaq. Es ist ein Test für den Erfolg der KI-Aktien.

nzz.title: Fussball-WM 2026: Spannungsgeladene Konfrontation statt komplexe Spielzüge
nzz.description: Die Ästhetik des Spiels hat sich über die Jahrzehnte stets gewandelt. Nun sind wir wieder in eine neue Ära eingetreten. Die Schweizer Nati hat sich wie kaum ein anderes Team daran angepasst.

nzz.title: Ein Quantencomputer, der aus seinen Fehlern lernt
nzz.description: Google-Forscher haben eine Technik der künstlichen Intelligenz verwendet, um Fehler in einem Quantenprozessor in Echtzeit zu beheben. Im Gegensatz zu früher kann der Computer nun auch weiterrechnen, während er sich selbst korrigiert.

nzz.title: Vom Schreiben der Wahrheit in Island – Jón Kalman Stefánsson ist mit seinem neuen Roman ein irrwitziges Kunststück gelungen
nzz.description: Mit «Himmelskörper am Rande der Welt» beweist der isländische Schriftsteller Jón Kalman Stefánsson seine überragenden Qualitäten. Es geht um ein Massaker an spanischen Walfängern, aber noch stärker um haarsträubende intime Verwicklungen und erotische Verfehlungen.

nzz.title: «Israel existiert nicht» und «Joe Biden ist ein Vergewaltiger» – Darializa Avila Chevalier steht exemplarisch für die Radikalisierung bei den US-Demokraten
nzz.description: Die 32-Jährige hatte ein Erweckungserlebnis in Palästina. Dann konvertierte sie zum Islam – und nun setzte sie sich bei den New Yorker Vorwahlen für das Repräsentantenhaus durch

nzz.title: Die letzte Reise von Ayatollah Ali Khamenei
nzz.description: Nach einer tagelangen Trauerreise durch Iran und den Irak wird Irans oberster Führer Ali Khamenei am Donnerstag beigesetzt. Karten, Satellitenbilder und Drohnenaufnahmen zeichnen den Weg des Trauerzugs nach, der weit mehr ist als ein Staatsbegräbnis.

observador.title: Uma gaffe de Bugalho ou um recuo do PSD?
observador.description: O PSD anunciou que queria ouvir ex-ministros socialistas sobre a imigração. Dez dias depois, esses nomes desapareceram. Rui Pedro Antunes explica o que aconteceu.

observador.title: As notícias das 4h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: 3h. EUA atacam Irão pela segunda noite consecutiva
observador.description: Teerão avisa que a resposta será de grande escala. Ainda, o Chega apresentou esta noite novas alterações à chamada lei das burcas.

observador.title: 2h. Chega apresentou alterações à lei das burcas
observador.description: O partido de André Ventura diz ter garantias de aprovação do PSD. Ainda, o ministro da Educação afasta preocupações com a correção dos exames nacionais.

observador.title: 1h. Mais de mil pessoas em protesto em Almada
observador.description: Os moradores criticam a degradação da rede de abastecimento e acusam o município de falta de investimento. Ainda, Os EUA estão a atacar o Irão pela segunda noite consecutiva.

observador.title: Nos 250 anos da "Nova Roma"
observador.description: Lamento informar as mediáticas Cassandras que, 250 anos volvidos, o Congresso e o Supremo, bem como a divisão de poderes, continuam de saúde nos Estados Unidos do “pior dos césares”

observador.title: O século XXI é o mais pindérico de sempre?
observador.description: Porque a literatura anda tão chata? E onde foram parar os grandes filmes? Já não há estreias de jeito no teatro? E exposições a não perder? Há dois suspeitos, que não são os do costume.

observador.title: Se eles pensam e logo existem
observador.description: Foram os grandes modelos de linguagem a surpresa com que ninguém contava e que haveria de colocar o filósofo de regresso ao centro desta ágora inesperada.

observador.title: Caso a caso
observador.description: Um país livre e democrático é governado com base em normas universais. Em Portugal, exibem-se os privilégios selectivos.

observador.title: 00h. Ministro: 65% dos exames nacionais estão corrigidos
observador.description: Fernando Alexandre assegura que o processo de correção decorre de forma tranquila, apesar dos problemas iniciais. Ainda, mais de mil pessoas protestaram em Almada contra as falhas de água.

observador.title: Um Prémio Nobel para pensar Portugal
observador.description: Sobre o estudo encomendado ao Prémio Nobel da Economia de 2024, James A. Robinson, acompanhado pelo economista português Nuno Palma.

observador.title: Portugal resolveu tudo
observador.description: Portugal não está em declínio. Está em negação. E a diferença importa porque a segunda é uma escolha.

observador.title: Vivemos como se estivéssemos sozinhos
observador.description: Quando começamos a normalizar pequenas faltas de consideração pelos outros, estamos também a normalizar a sociedade em que aceitamos viver.

observador.title: Luís Montenegro vs. Roberto Martinez
observador.description: O voo de regresso de Montenegro, depois da derrota da Seleção, terá sido pesado. Imagino-o a pensar : "Será que estou com a estratégia certa? Será que ando só a passar a bola para o lado?".

observador.title: Agostinho da Silva e o Portugal idealizado por Camões
observador.description: A “grande façanha” de Portugal foi, precisamente, ter conquistado e mantido, “através de sangue o fogo”, dentro desse “todo” peninsular, a sua “independência”.

observador.title: God save the King
observador.description: Este artigo podia ser sobre futebol, mas não é. Podia ser sobre Cristiano Ronaldo, mas também não é. É sobre Portugal, e sobre a forma como olhamos para aqueles que atingem um nível de excelência.

observador.title: Juiz ordena libertação de fundos que Trump deve a Carroll
observador.description: Decisão surge mais de três anos depois de Carroll ter vencido Trump num processo por abuso sexual e difamação. Menos de uma hora após ordem judicial, Presidente norte-americano apresentou recurso.

observador.title: Vítimas de tráfico humano deixam de ser punidas
observador.description: Chega absteve-se. PSD e Livre introduziram alterações após críticas do Observatório do Tráfico e da CNPD. Novas regras incluem vítimas de escravidão.

spiegel.title: Disneys »Vaiana« neu im Kino: Warum muss heute aus jedem Animationsfilm ein Realfilm werden?
Taylor Swift und Travis Kelce: Fans zahlen für Abfall von Hochzeit - »New York City Garbage«
spiegel.description: Der Hype um die Hochzeit von Taylor Swift und Travis Kelce war riesig, davon wollte auch ein New Yorker Künstler profitieren: Er bot Abfall vom Eventgelände an, darunter Zigarettenstummel und einen Ovulationstest.

spiegel.title: News: VW-Stellen in Gefahr, Iran-USA-Krieg, Ajatollah Ali Khamenei, Beerdigung, Kai Wegner
spiegel.description: Der Volkswagen-Aufsichtsrat berät über Stellenabbau und Werksschließungen. Der Krieg zwischen den USA und Iran geht weiter. Und: Berlins Regierender Bürgermeister Wegner muss bangen. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagmorgen.

spiegel.title: Augenlasern: Für wen sich eine OP wirklich lohnt – und welche Risiken es gibt
spiegel.description: Eine Sehunschärfe lässt sich heutzutage schnell und einfach weglasern. Doch immer wieder kommt es bei Eingriffen zu Komplikationen. Wie sich Risiken vermeiden lassen.

spiegel.title: Therapie gegen Höhenangst: Wie ich meine Panik überwunden habe
spiegel.description: In die Tiefe blicken? Zwischen Himmel und Erde schweben? Ein Albtraum. Also verabrede ich mich mit einer Therapeutin am Sessellift.

spiegel.title: Iran-Krieg: USA melden Attacken auf Iran – Regime greift Kuwait und Bahrain
spiegel.description: Die USA greifen nach eigenen Angaben erneut Ziele in Iran an – und Donald Trump droht mit »noch Schlimmerem«. Teheran reagiert bereits: Kuwait und Bahrain geraten unter Beschuss.

spiegel.title: Graham Platner: US-Senatskandidat gibt nach Skandalen auf
spiegel.description: Sexuelle Übergriffe, ein Nazi-ähnliches Tattoo, fragwürdige Posts: Der demokratische Senatskandidat Graham Platner aus Maine hat seine Kampagne nach einer Serie von Vorwürfen beendet. Für seine Partei kommt das zur Unzeit.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM-Finale erstmals mit Halbzeitshow: Justin Bieber gesellt sich zu Madonna, Shakira, Coldplay und Co.
spiegel.description: Das WM-Finale bekommt erstmals eine Halbzeitshow, Fifa-Präsident Infantino schwärmt von der »größten Bühne aller Zeiten«. Neben Madonna, Shakira und BTS hat nun auch Justin Bieber zugesagt. Damit wird eine Frage immer drängender.

spiegel.title: Mending in Rheinland-Pfalz: Polizei rettet Männer aus Lava-Tunnel
spiegel.description: Mitten in einem erkalteten Lavastrom spannt sich unter der Stadt Mendig ein Netz von Felsenkellern – in 32 Meter Tiefe. Eine Gruppe von Männern betrat das Areal trotz Verbot und verlor die Orientierung. Zahlreiche Helfer mussten anrücken.

spiegel.title: Nato-Gipfel in Ankara: Friedrich Merz bekommt von Recep Tayyip Erdoğan Revolver geschenkt
spiegel.description: Was könnte ein passendes Geschenk für Nato-Gipfelteilnehmer sein? Gastgeber Recep Tayyip Erdoğan hat sich offenbar Gedanken gemacht und seine Gäste mit einem Revolver ausgestattet – samt Namensgravur und Munition.

spiegel.title: Iran: Warum Teheran jetzt einen neuen Krieg mit den USA riskiert
spiegel.description: Iran riskiert einen neuen Krieg mit den USA und US-Präsident Trump kündigt das Abkommen für die Waffenruhe auf. Warum gerade jetzt?

spiegel.title: ICE-Einsatz behindert: Ehemalige Richterin Hannah Dugan entgeht Haftstrafe
spiegel.description: Als Bezirksrichterin in Wisconsin soll sie einem Einwanderer bei der Flucht vor ICE-Einsatzkräften geholfen haben. Nun erging das Strafmaß für Hannah Dugan. Weil sie sonst eine »gute Person« sei, muss sie nicht ins Gefängnis.

spiegel.title: U19-EM: DFB-Elf besiegt Ukraine dank Francis Onyeka – nun Finale gegen Spanien
spiegel.description: Vor zwölf Jahren führte Joshua Kimmich eine deutsche U19 zum EM-Titel. Nun soll das wieder gelingen: Nach einem knappen Sieg über die Ukraine steht Deutschland im Endspiel. Dort wartet Topfavorit Spanien.

Now, researchers from the University of Osaka have developed a technique sensitive enough to capture this cell-by-cell diversity within tissues with unprecedented precision and stability. Their study is published in the journal Analytical Chemistry.

phys-org.title: How economic expectations and political polarization influence fertility rates and the number of marriages
phys-org.description: The University of Barcelona participated in a study that uses an unexpected change of government in Spain—the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party (PSOE) defeated the PP, against the odds, in the March 2004 general election—to examine whether changes in economic expectations affected births, abortions and marriages.

phys-org.title: Catching hydrogen in the act: Tracking the absorption process over time
phys-org.description: If you're looking for hydrogen on the elemental chart, it won't take you long to find it. It is right there at the beginning, the lightest possible material. One electron, one proton, one neutron. Simple, minimalistic, the Marie Kondo of the elemental chart, but with enormous potential in terms of possible technological applications.

phys-org.title: Planting the future: Researchers put AI to work on the farm
phys-org.description: Farmers are getting more tools in their toolbox, thanks to new research from the University of Missouri that shows how they can tweak planting practices to make the most of every acre.

phys-org.title: Why some glasses break suddenly while others deform smoothly
phys-org.description: If a liquid is cooled slowly to its freezing point, it becomes a crystal in which the constituent particles are arranged in an ordered pattern. In contrast, when the liquid is cooled very quickly, the particles are unable to arrange themselves in an ordered fashion, and it becomes glass. Glassy materials are all around us in everyday life. Common examples include window glass, certain metal alloys, polymers, foams, gels and even soft materials like emulsions and colloids.

phys-org.title: Should a chatbot manage your bank account? Probably not, according to analysis
phys-org.description: When it comes to managing your personal finances, you may want to stick with your accountant before turning to artificial intelligence, according to a new study from the University of Georgia.

phys-org.title: Satellites are transforming biodiversity monitoring for global nature targets, but major gaps remain
phys-org.description: A new scientific review outlines how satellites and other remote sensing technologies are increasingly shaping how biodiversity and ecosystem health can be monitored at scale—offering new opportunities for countries reporting under international nature targets, while also underscoring important limitations.

phys-org.title: Slowing Atlantic current could fuel stronger California atmospheric rivers by century's end
phys-org.description: A slowing Atlantic Ocean current is projected to intensify powerful storms in California while reducing snowfall over Greenland, according to a recent University of California, Riverside study. The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) works like a giant conveyor belt in the ocean, moving warm water from the tropics northward to heat places like Europe, then cycling the cooled, denser water back south along the ocean floor. phys-org.title: South African fynbos soil delivers a new species of soil bacterium
phys-org.description: Microbiologists from Stellenbosch University in South Africa have discovered a previously unknown bacterial genus within the phylum Acidobacteriota. It is the first genus from this phylum to be described from Southern Africa.

phys-org.title: Primordial mini-moons may explain meteorite composition
phys-org.description: A new Southwest Research Institute-led study proposes a solution to a longstanding puzzle in planetary science: What caused the concentration, assembly, and preservation of millimeter-sized, spherical mineral grains within the parent bodies of the most common meteorites? The work is published in the journal Science Advances.

phys-org.title: Brown howler monkeys rest more on long, hot days and when feeding on leaves
phys-org.description: The daily movements of brown howler monkeys (Alouatta guariba) in the forest are determined by an interplay of environmental, behavioral and social factors. This is one of the conclusions of a study conducted in Brazil and published in the International Journal of Primatology. The study may guide conservation efforts for the species.

phys-org.title: New deep-sea measurements show how the ocean floor forms
phys-org.description: The first-known direct observations of a seafloor spreading event at a mid-ocean ridge in the Indian Ocean are presented in Nature. The observations offer insight into how new oceanic crust is created.

phys-org.title: Decoding of one of nature's largest enzymes reveals electron flow behind biological methane production
phys-org.description: A research team at Marburg University has investigated one of the largest enzyme complexes found in nature to date and deciphered its remarkable structure. Under the supervision of Dr. Jan Schuller, Ph.D. student Sophia Paul from the Center for Synthetic Microbiology (SYNMIKRO) was able to characterize the so-called heterodisulfide reductase super-assembly in detail. phys-org.title: Nine out of 10 Brazilian cities have experienced climate-related disasters over the past three decades
phys-org.description: Extreme weather events are becoming increasingly frequent and severe. The El Niño predicted for 2026–2027 is one such event. These events have caused environmental, economic and social impacts in Brazil, requiring specific public policies. To transform scientific data into a foundation for developing prevention, adaptation and mitigation measures, a group of Brazilian researchers has analyzed approximately 60,000 records of hydrogeological disasters in Brazil between 1991 and 2024. Their results

phys-org.title: Europe risks a pollinator crisis, researchers warn
phys-org.description: Europe risks a severe crisis if the decline of wild pollinators continues. This is the key message of a new white paper prepared by 135 researchers from eight research consortia, including the projects BUTTERFLY, RestPoll, ProPollSoil and PolinERA, all involving researchers from Aarhus University. Among the authors are Claus Rasmussen, Martin Hvarregaard Thorsøe, James Williams, Johan Axelman and Chris Topping from the Department of Agroecology. The work is published in Zenodo.

new-sci.description: A drug that softens the ovaries helped mice and rats conceive more easily at an older age, and produce more pups

new-sci.title: Why Schrödinger's 1944 classic What Is Life? still feels prescient
new-sci.description: Pioneer of quantum mechanics Erwin Schrödinger's look at living organisms is one of the most influential popular-science books of the 20th century. So how does it hold up today, asks Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

new-sci.title: Lambs born via IVF using highly immature eggs in major breakthrough
new-sci.description: Lambs have been born using an experimental form of IVF that coaxes immature eggs to become mature ones. This could boost the number of eggs available for fertilisation and improve IVF success rates

new-sci.title: The allergy culprit histamine also boosts our memory
new-sci.description: A drug that raises levels of histamine – the chemical that causes allergy symptoms – in the brain boosts our memory by around 10 per cent

new-sci.title: Salt batteries are about to shake up EVs and grid storage
new-sci.description: Today, most rechargeable batteries are made from lithium ions, but sodium-ion alternatives could make battery tech much cheaper and offer other advantages

new-sci.title: How extreme heat affects the body – and the best ways to cope
new-sci.description: A short spell in a heat chamber at the University of Brighton showed Alec Luhn that his body is not adapted to high temperatures – but regular exposure can train the body to respond more effectively

new-sci.title: Peter Shor’s algorithm could break the internet – but he's not worried

new-sci.title: Does time come from the entire universe running computations?
new-sci.description: Explaining the passage of time has been a gnarly problem in physics basically forever, but physicist and computer scientist Stephen Wolfram has a radical proposal for where it comes from. He discussed his ideas on time – and what they mean for free will – with reporter Leah Crane

new-sci.title: The strange metals forcing us to rethink how electricity really works
new-sci.description: Some 40 years ago, physicists noticed certain metals were conducting electricity in a bizarre way no one could explain. New answers to how and why this happens are forcing us to question how electricity flows

new-sci.title: Chris Packham: 'I'd throw myself in front of a T. Rex to be consumed'
new-sci.description: As Chris Packham gears up for his new TV show, Evolution, he tells Penny Sarchet why understanding the latest evolutionary science is so important if we are to truly appreciate the natural world - and how he would happily die at the hands of a Tyrannosaurus rex

new-sci.title: 5 graphs that show how heatwaves are getting more dangerous
new-sci.description: Longer-lasting hot spells and high temperatures at night are making it harder to cope, leading to thousands more deaths from extreme heat

new-sci.title: Collapse of AMOC ocean current may already be locked in
new-sci.description: The fate of the Atlantic Ocean current that keeps Europe’s climate warm depends on our carbon emissions and the rate of ice melt from Greenland, but there is a chance that a shutdown is already inevitable

new-sci.title: Ovary identity shift after menopause may contribute to inflammation
new-sci.description: We used to think post-menopausal ovaries sat inert in the body, but evidence from mice suggests they may instead turn into an organ with a role in inflammation

new-sci.title: Bumblebee facial movements give clues to their inner lives
new-sci.description: A series of experiments shows that bees respond differently to tastes depending on their internal states, hinting that they have something akin to our emotions

new-sci.title: Artefacts hint at cultural exchange between Neanderthals and humans
new-sci.description: A cave on the Turkish Mediterranean coast was inhabited first by Neanderthals and then Homo sapiens, but the continuity of tools and personal objects suggests there was some sharing of culture between the two species

new-sci.title: How healthy is your brain? We now know how to find out
new-sci.description: In our efforts to keep our brains healthy, how do we know what is working? Helen Thomson explores a new generation of tests that can reveal whether our efforts are paying off

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: How Argentina Can Protect Its Resource Wealth
proj-syn.description: Alaska, Norway, and Chile recognized the economic and political risks that accompany commodity booms and established sovereign wealth funds to preserve their resource revenues. Argentina’s hydrocarbon- and lithium-rich provinces should learn from their experience.

proj-syn.title: Reinventing Development Finance
proj-syn.description: Faced with shrinking concessional finance and rising borrowing costs, Rwanda has worked with the World Bank Group to leverage limited public funds and risk-sharing instruments to unlock private capital at scale and on affordable terms. It's an arrangement holding important lessons for low-income countries that must do more with less.

proj-syn.title: Mamdani’s American Dream
proj-syn.description: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s Independence Day address was a perfect example of ideology in the positive sense of the term. It overturned both the right-wing populist narrative of the United States and the left-wing "woke" critique with a vision that has the potential to mobilize a majority.

proj-syn.title: How Vulnerable Are US Financial Markets?
proj-syn.description: Fueled by more than $1 trillion in borrowed money and rising leverage across the financial system, US stock markets may have entered bubble territory. Two developments could trigger a sharp correction: higher interest rates and a loss of confidence in the handful of tech giants driving the AI boom.

proj-syn.title: Concessional Finance Is Needed More Than Ever
proj-syn.description: As debt burdens rise and climate shocks intensify, sustainable financing mechanisms are becoming indispensable. The Islamic Development Bank’s new concessional fund offers a promising model for mobilizing the resources needed to protect development gains and invest in resilience.

proj-syn.title: Ruling Class Clowns
proj-syn.description: By the end of the 19th-century in the US, it was clear to all interested observers that market power did not automatically or even easily translate into political capital and cultural authority. That is why, unlike the oligarchs of our time, certain Gilded Age capitalists learned how to become a ruling class.

proj-syn.title: The Missing Ingredient for European Tech Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: Europe’s dependence on US technology companies is both an economic challenge and a strategic vulnerability. The European Union’s new Tech Sovereignty Package is a step in the right direction, but without equally ambitious efforts to curb market concentration, it is bound to fall short.

proj-syn.title: In Praise of the World Cup’s Little Guys
proj-syn.description: In a world of great-power rivalry and hyper-scaling tech behemoths, you would be forgiven for thinking that the bulky bully always has the edge. But as this year's World Cup has shown repeatedly, you would be wrong.

proj-syn.title: Inside Ukraine’s Game-Changing Drone Industry
proj-syn.description: In recent months, Ukrainian drones have successfully struck dozens of sites deep inside Russia, targeting the oil industry, weapons plants, and logistics hubs. But while Ukraine has developed a world-leading military technology to defend itself from a much larger aggressor, drones will not be enough to end the war.

proj-syn.title: Just Say No to Remote Work
proj-syn.description: Even during the immediate post-pandemic period, when evidence on the labor-market effects of remote work was scant, there was a strong case to be made for going into the office, especially for younger workers. And now, multiple new studies have vindicated this intuition.

proj-syn.title: There Is Only One Acceptable Path for Designer Babies
proj-syn.description: Genetic-engineering tools with which to design one's progeny already exist, and they are being made even more potent with AI—at least for those who can afford such services. In the absence of policy interventions, we will be hurtling toward a tiered society in which economic privileges become biological advantages.

proj-syn.title: The Democratic Turkey NATO Needs
proj-syn.description: At NATO's upcoming summit in Ankara, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan will seek to portray his country as stable, confident, and essential to Western security. But only the last one is true, which is why the restoration of democracy in Turkey is more than a domestic concern.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup as It Should Be
proj-syn.description: While Donald Trump was widely expected to lord over this year’s World Cup, which the United States is co-hosting with Mexico and Canada, it has turned out not to be his scene. National teams populated with immigrants, and small-town America’s embrace of the event, go against everything Trump’s MAGA movement stands for.

proj-syn.title: The Real Threat to NATO
proj-syn.description: The greatest challenge to NATO comes not from its adversaries but from within. As its leaders gather in Ankara on July 7-8, they should focus less on military capabilities than on reinvigorating the alliance's founding strategic philosophy, centered on democratic legitimacy, human rights, and the rule of law.

proj-syn.title: How the EU Can Lead the Rest of the West
proj-syn.description: While Europe is not just another middle power, nor is it a great power with sufficient economic, military, and geopolitical clout to dictate terms on the global stage. Instead, Europe is the ideal candidate to convene and lead a group of like-minded middle powers, not as a US-style hegemon, but as a first among equals.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Face the World on Its Own
proj-syn.description: Under pressure from Russian aggression—which has reached its full expression in the ongoing war against Ukraine—and an increasingly hostile US administration, Europe urgently needs to make progress toward a defense union. But that will require Franco-German leadership of the kind that is not yet on offer.

proj-syn.title: How Safe Are Today’s Blockbuster Tech Stocks?
proj-syn.description: Today’s wave of mega-IPOs has unleashed a wave of analogies to past booms. While no analogy is perfect, an especially apposite—and sobering—case may be what followed Nippon Telegraph and Telephone’s IPO in February 1987.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s AI Dolce Vita?
proj-syn.description: Glacial growth, aging welfare states, and a shortage of centrist leaders suggest Europe faces a major debt crisis in the years ahead. But its emphasis on leisure over work could become a decisive advantage, positioning the continent as the leading model for thriving in an age of AI-driven abundance.
